providers.title: Influence and Fourier weights
providers.scope: sum over S containing i of hhat(S)^2 = sigma^2 I_i(h), and sum |S| hhat(S)^2 = sigma^2 I(h).
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Margulis-Russo formula
providers.scope: For increasing h, the derivative of E_p h in p is the total influence I_p(h).
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Biased hypercontractivity
providers.scope: With rho = sigma/4, ||T_rho g||_4 <= ||g||_2 on every finite biased product space.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Low-degree projections
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: A low-degree estimate (OpenAI)
providers.scope: If every influence of a Boolean h is at most I(h)/m, the Fourier weight of degrees 1 to sigma log m / 64 is at most m^(-1/4) I(h).
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Averaging over a restriction
providers.scope: Averaging restricted Fourier weights and influences over the fixed coordinates gives the corresponding sums for the original function.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The block estimate (OpenAI)
providers.scope: For a symmetric f and a random m-block B, the weight of supports meeting F_B in 1 to k edges is at most (2m/n) m^(-1/4) I(f).
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Capturing low degrees (OpenAI)
providers.scope: For log n >= 16 and m = floor(sqrt n), the Fourier weight of degrees 1 to k^2/2 is at most 4 m^(-1/4) I(f).
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Variance and influence for graph properties (OpenAI)
providers.scope: Var_p(f) <= 2^17 I_p(f) / (log n)^2 for every vertex-symmetric Boolean f and every p.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The Friedgut-Kalai conjecture (OpenAI)
providers.scope: Every nontrivial increasing graph property has p_(1-eps) - p_eps <= 2^19 log(1/(2 eps)) / (log n)^2.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The block estimate for hypergraphs
providers.scope: For an m-block with m >= r+1, the restricted low-degree weight is at most m^(-1/4) (rm/n) I_p(f).
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Capturing a hypergraph support
providers.scope: A support with at most (k/r)^(r/(r-1)) edges meets a random block in 1 to k edges with probability at least m/(2n).
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Variance and influence for hypergraph properties (OpenAI)
providers.scope: Var_p(f) <= C_r I_p(f) / (log n)^(r/(r-1)) for every r-uniform hypergraph property and every p.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Hypergraph thresholds (OpenAI)
providers.scope: Increasing r-uniform hypergraph properties have threshold width at most 2 C_r log((1-eps)/eps) / (log n)^(r/(r-1)).
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review
